tasks.short: Recommend facility locations and oversee renovations, balancing capacity, cost, disruption, and operational needs.

steps.what: Agree capacity needs, operational requirements, budget limits, and acceptable disruption.
Gather current occupancy, operating costs, staffing totals, and throughput records.
Inspect candidate premises or renovation areas with operational and technical specialists.
Review emailed designs, quotations, exclusions, and supplier delivery constraints.

loop.input: Supplier proposals, including quotations, layout descriptions, exclusions, and delivery terms.
loop.output: Offer notes with comparable fields, source passages, and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate amounts, currencies, dates, and totals deterministically. Reviewer confirms exclusions and scope comparability.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per proposal; unreadable or conflicting passages go to the facilities manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier formats and scope descriptions vary. Structured submissions use direct field mapping where available.

steps.what: Compare options for total cost, capacity, timing, disruption, and operational risk.
Write the recommended option, supporting assumptions, alternatives, and proposed delivery approach.

loop.input: Reviewed option appraisal, source evidence, and the operations manager's chosen recommendation.
loop.output: Investment recommendation covering costs, assumptions, alternatives, disruption, and unresolved risks.
loop.check: Insert figures directly from the appraisal. Require source references and manager review of every substantive claim.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims remain marked for human completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies the structure, but each site's trade-offs need a short narrative.

steps.what: Approve, reject, or request changes to the proposed investment.
Approve supplier awards and contractual commitments within delegated authority.
Coordinate contractors and department heads around access, sequencing, disruption, and emerging problems.
Record milestones, spending, open defects, and follow-up actions.
Inspect completed works and accept handover subject to specialist sign-offs and outstanding defects.

tasks.design: Configure a facility project template in the {PROJECT}, with approval records and links to evidence in the {DOCS}; a small integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins aggregate staffing, throughput, and costs from the {HCM}, {OPS_SYSTEM}, and {ERP}. A deterministic appraisal calculates comparable costs and scenarios, while bounded model loops extract proposal terms and draft the manager's recommendation. People retain site inspections, investment decisions, supplier commitments, coordination, and handover acceptance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Projects are infrequent, proposals differ, and site knowledge sits with several specialists. Connecting operational records and maintaining a reusable appraisal often cost more than preparing another bespoke workbook.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors, validation, and appraisal templates. Bounded extraction and drafting can handle variable proposal text; neither requires a new capability breakthrough.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden building defects, permit dependencies, contractual exclusions, and disruption estimates need specialist judgement. Use aggregate staffing data under GDPR; employee consultation and approvals depend on national rules and the proposed workplace changes.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing whether a site will work in practice, negotiating workable compromises, and accepting responsibility for capital and operational consequences.

ambition.what: Quarterly facility capacity and lease-option review.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into assembling comparisons and writing papers; more goes into site feasibility and resolving operational trade-offs. Investment and contractual decision rights remain within existing delegations.

reach.task: Compare the facility investment with other capital priorities.
reach.learn: Discounted cash flow, downside scenarios, capital constraints, and investment approval thresholds.

evidence.claim: A reusable appraisal, record integration, and configured project workflow are plausible deterministic building blocks; estimates require customer validation.
Board Intelligence Report Writer drafts structured papers from management documents. This supports the recommendation-drafting component, not facility selection.
Copilot in Power BI summarises reports and answers data questions. The digest warns that unprepared data models give inaccurate answers.
Physical inspections, technical acceptance, and capital trade-offs remain human work; the digest provides no documented facility-project automation case.

assumptions: Steps describe a representative project; location selection and renovation share an appraisal and delivery process but need different technical evidence.
Time shares cover the end-to-end task across participating roles and repeated coordination cycles, not only the operations manager's desk time.
Meetings and site visits take 54% of today's time, consistent with the supplied prior that judgement and coordination dominate.
A viable {PROJECT} configuration exists; building a replacement records application is unnecessary.
Qualified specialists supply technical assessments, permits, and completion certificates.
Remaining-time percentages and build-day ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Consent and access estimates include employee consultation where applicable; formal national processes may take longer and can overlap other work.
unknowns: Which facility decision is next, and whether selection, renovation, or both are in scope.
Available interfaces, data quality, and rights to use staffing, cost, occupancy, and throughput records.
Whether existing {PROJECT} templates and {ERP} connections can be configured directly.
Who approves investment, supplier commitments, scope changes, and handover at each value threshold.
Applicable national consultation, permitting, and workplace requirements.
Whether supplier proposals contain usable text and comparable scope.
Current project volumes, baseline effort, and enough reuse to justify ongoing upkeep.
research_questions: Which structured proposal fields capture the most consequential omissions across facility projects?
Which appraisal assumptions most often explain differences between approved budgets and completed-project costs?
Can existing {PROJECT} configuration support the required approvals and evidence links without custom development?
new_work: Check extracted proposal exclusions, assumptions, and scope differences.
Review generated recommendations and resolve unsupported claims.
Maintain cost mappings, appraisal formulas, approval thresholds, and project templates.
Handle failed imports, stale records, and missing specialist evidence.
Compare completed-project costs and disruption with the original appraisal.

role.altitude: The operations manager spends less time assembling facility papers and more time testing feasibility and coordinating delivery. Capital approval and contractual authority do not change automatically.
reach: Support the chief executive's capital allocation decisions with comparable facility scenarios.
skills_to_grow: Source-based review of extracted proposal terms
role.ambitious_version: Run a quarterly facility capacity and lease-option review that identifies viable choices before an urgent relocation or renovation becomes unavoidable.
